newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN to delay AGM for talks on rescue.
newsitem.headline: GAN to delay AGM for talks on rescue.

text.p: State-controlled insurer GAN will seek postponement of its annual shareholders' meeting to allow further talks with the European Commission aimed at winning approval for a massive capital injection, the new Socialist government said on Friday.
An early privatisation of GAN is regarded as a precondition of European Commission of approval of the 20 billion franc rescue package announced last February by the previous centre-right government.

The centre-right coalition, ousted in parliamentary elections on June 1, intended the capital injection to be a prelude to the privatisation this year of GAN and CIC, the regional banking group it controls.

The Socialist government has put privatisations on hold and the statement issued by the finance ministry made no mention of a sale of GAN, which ran up huge losses in recent years on property loans and insurance underwriting.
But the ministry said it was, "ready to bring this matter to a rapid conclusion in order to give GAN the means it needs."

GAN chairman Didier Pfeiffer has called a board meeting for June 17 to ask it to request the commercial court to allow the annual general meeting set for June 30 to be delayed, the ministry statement said.
The ministry said the delay was necessary to bring to fruition the talks with the European Commission.

French insurer AGF has shown strong interest in buying GAN's insurance operations to build up its presence in the sector following last year's mega-merger of Axa SA and Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP).

The previous government said the GAN bailout would not endanger France's efforts to cut its deficit to meet conditions for qualifying for a single European currency as it said it would get the money from other privatisations in 1996 and 1997.
